solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Board game taking place in Missouri academic institution

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: an event that is on is happening
MO is the postal abbreviation for the US state
short for polytechnic, a former type of British college

explanation.surface: Someone describes a board game tournament being held at a college in Missouri.
explanation.walkthrough: The state's abbreviation is split to hold the piece for 'taking place'. A poly was a British polytechnic, a college that has since mostly become a university.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous property-trading game played on a square track with dice and houses.

clue.text: Up in workshop, Alf dumps component of bike?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
the answer is said to be inside the following words, so look within them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word, the name and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A mechanic called Alf is throwing away parts in a workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'workshoP ALF DUMps' sits PALFDUM, which read upwards gives MUDFLAP. The question mark admits a mudflap is not essential to a bike.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudflap is a guard fitted behind a wheel, often found on bicycles as well as lorries, so it is one part of a bike.

clue.text: Newly drained, like a lake in Africa

indicators.note: a drained container has had its contents emptied out, leaving only the outside shell

blocks.note: the word with its middle emptied
as and like both mean similar to
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lake in Africa is described as having just been emptied of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly drained' reads like a description of the lake, but it tells you to empty the word Newly to its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyasa is the older name for Lake Malawi, a large body of water in the African Rift Valley.

clue.text: Wine very good, presumably rouge or rosé

blocks.note: PI is short for pious, very good in a religious sense
a red or pink wine is not white, and blanc is French for white

explanation.surface: A wine critic says a wine is very good and guesses it must be a red or a pink.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the answer is a white wine: rouge or rosé is 'not blanc', the French words fitting the wine theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot blanc is a white grape variety and the dry white wine made from it.

clue.text: Sign outside worker’s outhouse?

indicators.note: one thing outside another wraps around it, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A sign has been hung on the outside of a workman's shed.
explanation.walkthrough: The zodiac sign wraps round the insect. The apostrophe s in worker's stands for 'has', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against an existing wall, a kind of outbuilding; the question mark flags it as one example.

clue.text: Lemon fine with chop

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A cook prepares a fine lemon along with a chop of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Lemon looks like fruit next to a chop in the kitchen, but here it is slang for a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a lemon is something that turns out useless or a failure, just as a flop is.

clue.text: Left one remedy, reportedly a type of alcoholic drink

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so go by the sound rather than the spelling

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cure is a remedy, and the end of the drink's name is said the same way

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a strong drink as a cure, leaving one behind.
explanation.walkthrough: L and I are spelt normally; only the last part is a sound-alike, with the French-looking QUEUR pronounced like cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A liqueur is a sweet, flavoured spirit such as Cointreau, so it is one kind of strong drink.

clue.text: Musical instrument Scotsman found in Italian river

indicators.note: something found in a place is located inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Ian is a typically Scottish name
the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's musical instrument has turned up in an Italian river.
explanation.walkthrough: IAN placed inside PO gives PIANO. The Po and a Scot called Ian are both crossword staples.
explanation.definitionFit: The piano is a keyboard instrument whose strings are struck by hammers when keys are pressed.

clue.text: Approach section of hospital about new organ

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, as in about-turn, so the letters face the other way

blocks.note: a ward is a section of a hospital
N is the abbreviation for new
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A hospital ward deals with the arrival of a transplanted organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approach' could be read as a noun (a method), but here it is the verb, matching the phrasal verb in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw near is a phrasal verb meaning to come closer, exactly as approach does.

clue.text: Blue first-class quartz, half cut

indicators.note: with half of something cut away only the other half is left, so a word loses half its letters

blocks.note: A is the top grade, as in A1
a deletion: the first half of the word, its last three letters cut off

explanation.surface: A gem cutter praises some fine blue quartz that is only half cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Half cut sounds like gem-cutting, and is also British slang for drunk, but here it removes the back half of quartz.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is a light greenish-blue colour, named after the Latin word for water.

clue.text: Military campaign disturbed man and aircrew

indicators.note: something disturbed has been thrown out of its proper order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wartime operation has upset a soldier and the crew of a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of MAN and AIRCREW together rearrange to the answer; 'and' simply joins the two pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean War of 1853 to 1856 pitted Russia against Britain, France and the Ottoman Empire, a historic armed conflict.

clue.text: Smallest final involving England’s capital

indicators.note: a capital is the head or leading letter of a word, so take its opening letter
to involve something is to include it, so one piece is taken inside the other

blocks.note: last and final both mean coming at the end
the leading letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: A sports final includes the smallest team, playing in London.
explanation.walkthrough: England's capital looks like London, but capital here means capital letter, the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Least is the superlative of little, meaning of the lowest size or amount, as smallest does.

clue.text: Weapon destroyed depot protecting men

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken up, so its letters are scattered into a new order
to protect something is to shield it on all sides, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: taken as written
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A weapon has blown up an army depot while soldiers stand guard.
explanation.walkthrough: DEPOT rearranged to T PEDO wraps round OR. OR (other ranks) is a standard crossword way to clue men.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater missile fired from submarines or ships, so it is a weapon.

clue.text: Journalist probes friend with old aquatic vessel

indicators.note: a probe pushes into something, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: ED is short for editor
a pal is a friend
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A reporter investigates a friend who owns an old boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Journalist is clued by ED, short for editor, a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedalo is a small pleasure boat driven by foot pedals, common at seaside resorts and boating lakes.

clue.text: Party time aboard taxi for Thomas perhaps

indicators.note: a passenger aboard a vehicle is inside it, so one piece rides within the other

blocks.note: a do is a party
T is the abbreviation for time
Uber is the ride-hailing taxi company

explanation.surface: Someone called Thomas is partying in the back of a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas looks like a passenger, but refers to the apostle known as Doubting Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Thomas would not believe in the resurrection without proof, hence 'doubting Thomas'; 'perhaps' marks him as one example.

clue.text: Code of silence customer tacitly keeps

indicators.note: what a phrase keeps it holds within, so the letters are inside the words

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A customer quietly keeps a pledge of secrecy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tacitly means silently, which fits the surface theme neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Omertà is the Mafia's rule forbidding members from talking to police about crimes, a vow of silence.

clue.text: Perpetually young fool retains set exercise to begin with

indicators.note: what comes to begin with is at the start, so keep only the opening letter
to retain something is to hold onto it, so one piece is kept inside the other

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
jelly that sets is said to gel
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A youthful-looking fool insists on doing a set of exercises first.
explanation.walkthrough: Set looks like a noun, a set of exercises, but it is the verb meaning to firm up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageless describes someone who never seems to grow older, staying youthful forever.

clue.text: See, during crash, a meandering movement

indicators.note: something happening during an event falls within it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look or see
a slam is a loud crash

explanation.surface: A witness describes a car swerving about during a collision.
explanation.walkthrough: See is the old exclamation 'lo', as in 'lo and behold', a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A slalom is a zigzag course between poles, as in skiing, so it is a winding, weaving motion.

clue.text: Having a daily cycle, face carrying tea-making vessel?

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: a dial is the face of a clock
a tea urn is a large boiler for making tea

explanation.surface: A clock face holds a teapot, tying a daily routine to teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: Face here is a clock face, which fits the daily-cycle theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Diurnal means recurring every day or active during daytime, from the Latin for day.

clue.text: Amusing plaything entertains Romeo

indicators.note: a host entertains guests in their home, so one piece is taken in by the other

blocks.note: a doll is a toy
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A funny toy keeps a romantic young man amused.
explanation.walkthrough: R inside DOLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means humorous in a dry or quaint way, so it is a close synonym of funny.

clue.text: Consumed drinks on mountain ridge

indicators.note: to drink something is to take it in, so one piece is swallowed by the other

blocks.note: ate means consumed
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Climbers finish off their drinks up on a mountain ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Drinks looks like a noun but is the verb: the word for consumed swallows the word for on.
explanation.definitionFit: An arête is a sharp, narrow crest between two glacial valleys in mountain terrain.

clue.text: Icon making supremo jittery to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the following words is needed, so the letters lie within them

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A popular figure makes the boss nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: Icon reads like a celebrity, but it is the small digital symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An emoji is a small pictorial symbol used in texts and on screens, a type of digital icon.

clue.text: Cereal regularly used in local test

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so take every other letter

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A breakfast cereal is routinely used in a local taste test.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even letters of 'local test' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal grain, eaten as porridge or in muesli, so they are a kind of cereal crop.

clue.text: Breathing apparatus hit tricky problem

blocks.note: a blow is a hit
to be in a hole is to be in a difficult spot

explanation.surface: A diver's breathing equipment has hit a snag.
explanation.walkthrough: Apparatus suggests a machine, but the answer is the nostril on top of a whale's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A whale or dolphin breathes through its blowhole, so it serves as the animal's breathing organ.

clue.text: Learning actor’s part, hands must be reversed

indicators.note: the two hands are left and right, so swapping them exchanges those two letters

blocks.note: a role is an actor's part

explanation.surface: An actor learning a part is told to swap hands in a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The hands are R (right) and L (left); in ROLE they trade places, giving LORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lore is accumulated knowledge or tradition on a subject, as in folklore, so it means acquired knowledge.

clue.text: Ma and sister crunched colourful confectionery

indicators.note: something crunched is crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mother and daughter munch on brightly coloured sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Smarties are British sugar-coated chocolate buttons in many colours, unlike the American chalky candy of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarties are small sweets with candy shells in bright colours, a well-known British treat.
